evidence_items.locator: AI moves from on-the-side to built-in
evidence_items.explanation: The survey reports broad integration of coding assistants and agents. Together with the task and frequency details in e2, this meets the ordinary workflow interpretation of a big impact.

The section reports that 73% of coding-assistant or agent users use them daily. Reported applications include generating familiar code and debugging, showing actual programming integration rather than adoption intentions.

evidence_items.locator: Opening discussion of the updated productivity experiment
evidence_items.explanation: METR identifies selection and measurement problems in estimating productivity effects. This limits any stronger conclusion about speed gains but does not contradict substantial changes in coding workflows.

unresolved_gaps: The survey does not establish a representative population-wide productivity effect.
The evidence does not settle employment displacement, software quality, or the eventual scale of impact.
